race: Formula 1 MSC Cruises United States Grand Prix 2026

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Welcome back to The Race Weekend Podcast, because Austin has a title fight, a Ferrari threat, and one very bumpy track, and a weekend that feels bigger than the race.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Leclerc is the fresh practice headline, quickest with Verstappen right there, so the top three are already circling, and the headline is not just speed, it is timing.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: And Verstappen is not happy about the bumps, calling them unacceptable and out of control, which sets the mood.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: So that is our setup, a championship lead, a Ferrari high, and a Red Bull warning, all in one weekend.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Let's start with Kimi Antonelli, our number one pick, and the man carrying the title into Austin, and the pressure is already on.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: He is the championship leader, with consistent top five form, and Mercedes looks strong enough to hold onto it.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: But his Austin history is thin, just one race, and his best finish there is thirteenth, which is the obvious question.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: That is the quirk, a leader who has not proved himself on this exact layout, so we are trusting form over history.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: We still back him because the title is on the line, and he says he will just have fun, which is a nice line, and that mindset can win races.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Now Leclerc, our number two, is the one I trust here, because Ferrari form is real and the track suits him.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: This is his kind of place, with two podiums over two Austin races, and a best finish of first, so the history is clear.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: His average is second, and the fresh practice headline puts him fastest, so the data points right at him.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: That is not a coincidence, that is a circuit owner, and I am not buying any other name for the top step.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Then Verstappen, our number three, is the one nobody wants to ignore, because his Austin record is brutal, and he has done it before.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Three Austin races, three podiums, best first, and an average of one point seven, which is almost ridiculous.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Recent wins, dominant history, and Red Bull pace make him a live winner, even when Ferrari is quick on track.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: How do you beat that when Leclerc has the practice headline, the track history, and the Ferrari momentum?

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: You do not beat it, you just hope the bumps play to Red Bull, and that Verstappen stays calm enough to punish them.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: That is our deep cut, Leclerc owns the track, but Verstappen owns the result, and that is the real battle.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: I like that, two different kinds of history, one for pace, and one for wins, and that is why the top three is so tight.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: And Hamilton brings the other Ferrari angle, with top three overall form and solid recent results, so he is number four, and the car is finally showing it.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: He is our number four, and his own message is humility, which suits a man still chasing the big one.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Norris is number five, with that recent fourth, strong Austin history, and real McLaren pace to trust.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Russell is number six, second in the championship, but that recent ninth keeps him just behind Antonelli.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Piastri is number seven, with a recent fifth and that good balance between street and race pace, so he is on.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Hadjar, Lawson, and Lindblad fill the rest, with Red Bull pace, Racing Bulls consistency, and solid points hauls, and the mid pack is not sleeping.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Now the full top ten in one breath, Kimi Antonelli, Charles Leclerc, Max Verstappen, Lewis Hamilton, Lando Norris, George Russell, Oscar Piastri, Isack Hadjar, Liam Lawson, Arvid Lindblad.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Austin, title fight, bumpy track, and three drivers who all have a story to tell, so see you at the checkered flag, and the crowd is ready for drama.
